newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian cabinet works on balanced 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Latvian cabinet works on balanced 1998 budget.

text.p: Finance Minister Robert Zile on Tuesday said the cabinet was working on a draft 1998 state budget which would be balanced.

"The cabinet is expected today to agree on the draft 1998 budget determining a rough outline of expenditure and income targets for ministries, envisaging a balanced budget," Zile told a news conference.
"We expect the total budget to grow by some 9.9 percent," he added. The budget in 1997 was 2.6 billion lats.
Latvia, under the leadership of non-party businessman prime minister, Andris Shkele, drew up a balanced budget for 1997 after a near 40 million deficit in 1996.
The draft budget foresees a 50 percent rise in state investment, in line with the government programme, Zile said.
The ministry earlier said the final version of the state budget for 1998 should be ready by September.
He also said the finance ministry had drawn up a law to combine income and corporate tax in one package which brings the country closer to European Union norms.
But he said Latvia had still to work on getting excise tax in line with the EU and would consult first with Lithuania and Estonia to have more regional balance.
